description: Issue #962, acceptance criterion 6, made stack-neutral. The fix lets the reader cross a newline to reach its required `for key` tail; the hazard that carries is reaching too far and swallowing the statement on the next line. Every program here is already invalid -- each reader is deliberately INCOMPLETE -- but the statement that follows is independently valid, and losing it is how this class of fix silently changes what a program means. This fixture deliberately does NOT separate the fixed parser from the pre-fix one: measured at `e6281969`, all 10 diagnostics below are identical, because a reader that never crosses a newline cannot reach past one either. What it separates is the fixed parser from the FIRST DRAFT of this fix. Measured: removing the two-word lookahead makes the `for zzz 1` row report `zzz` instead of "end of line"; removing the `in`/`from` binder guard makes the `for key in`/`for key from` rows lose their loop entirely, in either case spelling. `for` is the one word the reader crosses a newline for that can also BEGIN a statement (`for-in-statement`/`for-range-statement`, `spec/grammar.md:130-131`), and `key` is a legal `binder` (`:388`), so `for key in …` and `for key from …` look exactly like this reader's tail while being loops. Each reader raises exactly one `ol-bad-token` anchored at the NEWLINE (`params.text` "end of line"); an anchor naming a word from the following line is the observable signature of a reader that reached past the newline it should have released. The additional diagnostic, on `1` at [60,9] -- ninth of the 10, not the last -- is the `for zzz 1` line being read on its own terms after the reader released it; its presence is part of the assertion, not noise. The reader operates on a dict, so Heritage also needs Data (`spec/conformance.md:305`).
